title: Your First Dashboard
text:
3.1 Load and summarise the data
This chunk goes at the top of the dashboard, before the first column. It runs once and shows nothing; every panel can use what it creates.

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# data: one row per county and year
oh <- read_csv("data/ohio_lung_cancer_1968_1988.csv",
               col_types = cols(GEOID = "c"))          # GEOID as text

# boundaries
oh_map <- counties(state = "OH", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# for the map: one row per county
by_county <- oh |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

oh_map <- left_join(oh_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# for the time series: one row per year
focus <- "Cuyahoga"                              # county to follow

by_year <- bind_rows(
  oh |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(area = "Ohio"),
  oh |> filter(county == focus) |>
    mutate(area = focus)
) |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

The same data, summarised twice: over the years for the map (by_county, 88 rows), and over the counties for the time series (by_year, one row per year for Ohio and one per year for Cuyahoga County). That is the whole idea of M1.
Check the join before going further: the number of counties without data should be zero.

sum(is.na(oh_map$SIR))                                 # should be 0

[1] 0

title: Your First Dashboard
text:
3.2 The map
The leaflet map of Exercise 4: the SIR, with the same classes and the same red–blue colours, so that the neutral class sits around 1.

breaks <- c(0, 0.5, 2/3, 0.9, 1/0.9, 1.5, 2, Inf)  # Exercise 4 classes
pal <- colorBin(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "RdBu")),
                domain = oh_map$SIR, bins = breaks)

leaflet(oh_map) |>
  addTiles() |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(SIR), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: SIR %.2f (%.0f observed, %.0f expected)",
                     NAME, SIR, Y, E),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~SIR, title = "SIR",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), opacity = 0.8)





Hover over a county: the label gives its observed and expected cases, so the reader can judge whether a dark colour rests on many cases or on a handful.

title: Your First Dashboard
text:
3.3 The time series
An ordinary ggplot: one line for Ohio, one for Cuyahoga County, and a dashed line at 1, as many cases as expected.

cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Ohio", focus))

p <- ggplot(by_year, aes(year, SIR, colour = area)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIR", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

p








One more line makes it interactive: hover for the values, drag to zoom, double-click to reset.

ggplotly(p)                                  # hover, zoom





Ohio’s SIR rose from 0.67 in 1968 to 1.32 in 1988. The expected cases use one set of rates for the whole period, so the map averages over this rise; in M2 the reader will pick the year.

title: Your First Dashboard
Your First Dashboard
text:
3.5 Put it together
Paste the chunks of §3.1–§3.4 under their ### panels. Two additions to the YAML header: theme: cosmo, the look of our course pages, and source_code: embed, a Source Code button in the corner, so that I can read your code from the dashboard itself. The whole file:
---
title: "Lung cancer in Ohio, 1968--1988"
output:
  flexdashboard::flex_dashboard:
    orientation: columns
    vertical_layout: fill
    theme: cosmo
    source_code: embed
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# data: one row per county and year
oh <- read_csv("data/ohio_lung_cancer_1968_1988.csv",
               col_types = cols(GEOID = "c"))          # GEOID as text

# boundaries
oh_map <- counties(state = "OH", cb = TRUE, year = 2020,
                   progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  st_transform(4326)                             # leaflet wants lon/lat

# for the map: one row per county
by_county <- oh |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)

oh_map <- left_join(oh_map, by_county, by = "GEOID")

# for the time series: one row per year
focus <- "Cuyahoga"                              # county to follow

by_year <- bind_rows(
  oh |> group_by(year) |>
    summarise(Y = sum(Y), E = sum(E), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(area = "Ohio"),
  oh |> filter(county == focus) |>
    mutate(area = focus)
) |>
  mutate(SIR = Y / E)
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Standardized incidence ratio (SIR) by county, 1968--1988

```{r map}
breaks <- c(0, 0.5, 2/3, 0.9, 1/0.9, 1.5, 2, Inf)  # Exercise 4 classes
pal <- colorBin(rev(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(7, "RdBu")),
                domain = oh_map$SIR, bins = breaks)

leaflet(oh_map) |>
  addProviderTiles("CartoDB.Positron") |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(SIR), fillOpacity = 0.8,
    color = "white", weight = 1,
    label = ~sprintf("%s: SIR %.2f (%.0f observed, %.0f expected)",
                     NAME, SIR, Y, E),
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 2, color = "black",
                                        bringToFront = TRUE)
  ) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = ~SIR, title = "SIR",
            labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 2), opacity = 0.8)
```

> SIR = observed / expected. Red: more cases than expected; blue: fewer.

Column {data-width=400}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### SIR by year (dashed line: as many cases as expected)

```{r timeseries}
cols <- setNames(c("black", "#B2182B"), c("Ohio", focus))

p <- ggplot(by_year, aes(year, SIR, colour = area)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "SIR", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()

ggplotly(p)                                  # hover, zoom
```

### Counties

```{r table}
oh_map |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  transmute(County = NAME, Observed = Y,
            Expected = round(E, 1), SIR = round(SIR, 2)) |>
  arrange(desc(SIR)) |>
  datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

> Data: Moraga (2019), Ch. 7. Boundaries: US Census Bureau, via `tigris`.

title: Your First Dashboard
text:
3.6 Render it
Save the file as dashboard.Rmd at the top of your repository, next to the data/ folder, and click Knit in RStudio (or run rmarkdown::render("dashboard.Rmd") in the Console). You get dashboard.html: one self-contained file that opens in any browser.






WarningKnit, not quarto render



Quarto does not know the flexdashboard format. Rendered with Quarto, the file comes out as an ordinary scrolling page, with the panel titles as headings. If your “dashboard” scrolls like a report, this is why.


That is M1: renderable from your repository.

title: Your First Dashboard
text:
3.7 Put it online (optional for M1)
Your exercises are a Quarto website published from docs/. Two entries in _quarto.yml add the dashboard to it:
project:
  type: website
  output-dir: docs
  render:
    - "*.qmd"          # Quarto renders the .qmd pages only
  resources:
    - dashboard.html   # and copies the knitted dashboard into docs/
Then, each time: Knit dashboard.Rmd, run quarto render, and commit and push with GitHub Desktop. The dashboard is at https://<username>.github.io/<repository>/dashboard.html. Add a link to it from index.qmd:
[My dashboard](dashboard.html)
